subject: Talk command
text: The Talk command is used to speak to townsfolk and shopkeepers when facing them directly next to them.

evidence.quote: The talk option is used to talk to the various townsfolk and shopkeepers you'll come across on your journey. Make sure you're facing the person and are RIGHT next to them, facing them, and then use this option. Otherwise, it'll say, "There is no one there."

subject: Status command
text: The Status command displays vital statistics including Name, Strength, Agility, Maximum HP, Maximum MP, Attack Power, Defense Power, Weapon, Armor, and Shield.

evidence.quote:
The status option allows you to see your character's vital stats...
Name: The Name of your character.
Strength: The strength of your character.
Agility: Your character's ability to stay alive.
Maximum HP: The maximum amount of hit points your character can have.
Maximum MP: The maximum amount of magic points your character can have.
Attack Power: How much damage your character can dish.
Defense Power: How much damage your character can take.
Weapon: The weapon your character is currently equipped with.
Armor: The piece of armor your character is currently equipped with.
Shield: The shield your character currently has on.

subject: Stairs command
text: The Stairs command moves the character up and down stairs when standing directly on top of the staircase.

evidence.quote: Used to go up and down stairs. When you're standing OVER and ON TOP OF the staircase, use this option. Otherwise, it'll say, "There are no stairs here."

subject: Search command
text: The Search command searches the ground for hidden items when standing on top of the target area.

evidence.quote: The search command is used to search the ground for something hidden. Use it on top of the area where you think something secret might be laying. If there is nothing there, it'll say, "[Your Character] searched the ground all about. But there found nothing."

subject: Spell command
text: The Spell command requires sufficient Magic Points to cast spells learned as the character levels up.

evidence.quote: The spell command is one that is used a little later in the game when your character gets high enough in level where it can use various kinds of spells. Select the spell you'd like to use, and if you have enough MPs, then you'll use it. Otherwise, it'll say, "[Your Character] cannot yet use the spell."

subject: Item command
text: The Item command displays inventory, which can only hold a limited amount of items.

evidence.quote: Use this option to see what items you have in your inventory. Be careful of how much you carry; your character can only carry a certain amount of items before you can't carry anything else. If you have no items available at the time, it'll say, "Nothing of use has yet been given to thee."

subject: Door command
text: The Door command opens doors when standing directly in front of them, sometimes requiring a key.

evidence.quote: This option allows you to pass through doors. (sometimes, you'll need a key). Walk directly in front of the door and then select this option to open the door. If there is no door in front of you, it'll say, "There is no door here."

subject: Take command
text: The Take command takes the contents of a treasure chest when standing directly on top of it, returning the item if inventory is full.

evidence.quote: This is the option to use if you want to take something out of a treasure chest. Walk directly on top of the treasure chest you'd like to open and select this option to take whatever is in the treasure chest as your own. (if your inventory is full, it'll put that item back in the treasure chest until you have room for it.) If you're not on top of a treasure chest, it'll say, "There is nothing to take here."

subject: Fight command
text: The Fight battle command attacks the enemy with the currently equipped weapon, occasionally resulting in critical damage or a complete miss.

evidence.quote: Choose this option, the main option you'll use in all fights, to attack your enemy with whatever weapon you have equipped. Do keep in mind that sometimes when you attack you'll do critical damage (or above average damage) to your target, and othertimes you'll miss completely.

subject: Run command
text: The Run command allows the player or enemies to attempt fleeing from battle.

evidence.quote: Choose this option if you feel you're over-powered in a fight, you think you're gonna perish, or if you just don't feel like fighting....(keep in mind that enemies can flee from battle as well, and often use their own run command when THEY themselves feel over-powered in battle).

subject: Battle Spell command
text: Using spells in battle requires having reached a sufficient level and consuming a certain amount of Magic Points.

evidence.quote: Once high enough in level, your character will start being able to utilize spells, both offensive and defensive spells, from healing spells for your character to offensive attack spells to use on your enemy....Each spell uses a certain amount of Magic Points (MP), so be weary of this.

subject: Battle Item command
text: The battle Item command lets the player use items in battle, though most items cannot be actively used during combat.

evidence.quote: Finally, the item command allows you to chose an item to use in battle, which is almost always some sort of healing herb. Most items can't be used actively in battle, so be aware of that when choosing certain items, otherwise you'll be hindered.

subject: Gold
text: Gold obtained from enemies and treasure chests is used to purchase armor, weapons, and items.

evidence.quote: Gold is the currency in the world of Dragon Warrior. You get it from enemies after winning a battle and in treasure chests as well. Use it to by armor, weapons and items throughout your journey.

subject: Experience
text: Experience points earned by winning battles determine when the character gains levels.

evidence.quote: Your experience (or experience points) determine when you're character is going to level up. The more experience points you have the more battles you've won, as experience points signify your success in battle; you only get them after winning a battle.

subject: Princess Gwaelin
text: Princess Gwaelin is King Lorik's daughter who is kidnapped by the Dragonlord and must be rescued.

evidence.quote: Princess Gwaelin is practically the whole first half of the game, as the Dragonlord kidnaps her and you have to first rescue her before facing off with the Dragonlord himself. She's King Lorik's daughter, and the love interest of the Hero.

subject: King Lorik
text: King Lorik rules Tantegel, is Princess Gwaelin's father, and saves the player's game.

evidence.quote: al you really know about him is that he runs the show in Tantegel, and that his daughter is Princess Gwaelin. You talk to him at length in the beginning and end of the game, but otherwise, your only contact with him is basically to save your game.

subject: Dragonlord
text: The Dragonlord kidnaps Princess Gwaelin and is fought at the end of the game in his castle at Charlock.

evidence.quote: The evil fiend bad guy of the game, the Dragonlord first kidnaps Princess Gwaelin, and then makes an attempt to take over the kingdom of Alefgard....All you know is that you have to eventually fight him in his castle at Charlock later in the game. At the end of the game, more precisely.

subject: Grass
text: Grasslands have a low encounter rate with mostly weak enemies and cause no terrain damage.

evidence.quote: The encounter rate on grasslands are low, and mostly low-grade enemies are commonly found on these pieces of land. You can travel quickest, with little interruption by enemies, by taking your cross-land routes over grass.
| GRASS       | LOW            | WEAK       | NONE         | N/A      |

subject: Heavy Grass
text: Heavy grass has a low-moderate encounter rate with weak to moderate enemies and inflicts no terrain damage.

evidence.quote: Similar to regular grass, optimal routes to and fro can be found on heavy grasses as well, although I found that the encounter rates are slightly higher on these dark green patches of grass. Enemies are a mix here as well.
| HEAVY GRASS | LOW-MODERATE   |WEAK-MOD.   | NONE         | N/A      |

subject: Forests
text: Forests feature a moderate encounter rate with moderate enemies and deal no damage.

evidence.quote: The forest has an increased encounter rate as well as some pretty tough enemies, combined with a few normal and weak enemies as well.
| FOREST      | MODERATE       | MODERATE   | NONE         | N/A      |

subject: Deserts
text: Deserts have a moderate encounter rate with moderate enemies and inflict no terrain damage.

evidence.quote: The deserts have similar encounter rates, I've found, to that of the forest. The monsters are a mixed bunch, usually specialized to the desert region.
| DESERT      | MODERATE       | MODERATE   | NONE         | N/A      |

subject: Hills
text: Hills feature slow travel speeds, an extremely high encounter rate, and mostly strong enemies.

evidence.quote: The hills are the most annoying land feature to traverse through. They have mostly strong enemies in them, and the encounter rate is extremely high. They also impede how fast you can travel.

subject: Poison Swamps
text: Poison swamps deal 1-2 HP of damage per step unless traversed with certain armors.

evidence.quote: The poison swamps have a pretty high encounter rate coupled with the fact that each step takes a certain amount (1-2 HPs) off each of your characters....Certain armors allow you to cross over these swamps unharmed, however.

subject: Magic Floors
text: Magic floors deal over 20 HP of damage per step unless the character wears Erdrick's Armor.

evidence.quote: Magic floors are a rare kind of floor that can only be traversed over by one who wears Erdrick's Armor. Otherwise, each step will take over 20 HPs from each of your characters.

subject: Mountains
text: Mountains cannot be traversed by any means.

evidence.quote: Mountains cannot be traversed over by any means, so you don't need to worry about them.

subject: Dungeon/Castle/Cave Floors
text: Dungeon, castle, and cave floors have moderate to high encounter rates with moderate to strong enemies and cause no step damage.

evidence.quote: The floors of dungeons, caves, and castles have moderate encounter rates and don't take any damage from your enemy.
|D/C/C FLOORS | MODERATE-HIGH  | MOD-STRONG | NONE         | N/A      |

subject: Hero
text: The Hero must rescue Princess Gwaelin, return her to King Lorik, gather Erdrick's armor and weapons, and face the Dragonlord.

evidence.quote: his quest in the game is to rescue Princess Gwaelin and return her to the King, King Lorik. Then he must have a final showdown with the Dragonlord. But not before he finds out his past connections with the great warrior Erdrick, travels the continent, and gathers the various pieces of his great ancestor's armor and weapons.
